verdict.rationale: Stripe's Shared Payment Tokens are scoped grants of a customer's payment method to a specific seller. The issuer sets usage_limits for currency, max_amount and expires_at, and can revoke the token at any time, with state-machine webhooks for each transition. The Link CLI also lets an agent obtain one-time-use virtual cards or SPTs from a customer-controlled wallet, with each spend request approved by the human, so the agent never holds the real card number. Missing for 10: an explicit user-configurable merchant allowlist (merchant scoping is only implied by the seller-specific grant, and Link virtual cards work at any merchant), independent hands-on corroboration that the limits are enforced, and general availability (ACS is private preview and limited to the US/select regions).
